discovery: First horizon-scale images of black holes (M87* and Sgr A*) with the Event Horizon Telescope

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / gravitation (black hole physics, very-long-baseline interferometry)
motivation: For decades black holes were the central theoretical laboratory where quantum mechanics and gravity meet, but their horizons stayed out of reach of direct observation. The Event Horizon Telescope made them observable. Falcke predicted that the shadow of Sgr A* could be imaged with millimetre VLBI. Doeleman led the development of the Earth-sized interferometer and produced the first detections of horizon-scale structure. Narayan's theory of radiatively inefficient accretion supplied the framework for modelling and interpreting the images. The 2019 image of M87* and the 2022 image of Sgr A* showed a bright ring around a central brightness depression. Its size matches the photon ring predicted by general relativity for Kerr black holes of the independently measured masses. Later polarimetric images revealed the magnetic field structure near the horizon. This work turns event horizons from mathematical constructs into objects we can measure, and it opens strong-field gravity to precise tests.
